about: Temperature: why the same question gets different answers. How AI works, part 6 (after Next word, Strawberry, Hallucinate, Noise, Memory). Puzzle film the viewer can try: ask a chatbot the same thing twice and get two answers. Why: for every next word the model has odds, and it rolls weighted dice over them; the dial on the dice is temperature (OpenAI API: 0 to 2, default 1, higher is more random, lower more focused; Hinton et al. 2015: higher T gives a softer distribution). It's on purpose: researchers found that chasing the likeliest text makes it bland and stuck in repetitive loops (Holtzman et al., ICLR 2020, GPT-2 'Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México' loop). Twist: even at temperature 0, Thinking Machines Lab (Sep 2025) sampled one prompt ('Tell me about Richard Feynman') 1,000 times on the open model Qwen3-235B and got 80 different completions, because server load changes batch size and the math rounds differently. Ends asking: same answer twice? Yes or no. Factory #10. Narration-led: the voice is recorded first and every visual beat is keyed to its word times.

lines.text: So why does ChatGPT give different answers?
Here's the trick: it rolls dice. On purpose.
Every next word has odds. Best pizza topping? Pepperoni gets 60%.
lines.say: Every next word has odds. Best pizza topping? Pepperoni gets sixty percent.

lines.text: Weighted dice, so mushrooms still win sometimes.
They come with a dial. It's called temperature.
Turn it down, and the favorite almost always wins.
Turn it up, and long shots get a chance.
Why not always pick the favorite?
Researchers tried. It got stuck repeating itself.
But at zero, a lab asked the same thing 1,000 times.
lines.say: But at zero, a lab asked the same thing a thousand times.

lines.text: 80 different answers. Busy servers round the math differently.
lines.say: Eighty different answers. Busy servers round the math differently.

lines.text: So ask yours twice. Same answer? Yes or no.
